title: Replication data for: climate warming-induced replacement of mesic beech by thermophilic oak forests will reduce the carbon storage potential in aboveground biomass and soil.

notes: We investigated carbon pools in soil and biomass together with soil chemical conditions along three transects in the natural ecotone from mesic beech forests to more xeric oak forests in western Romania with the aim to quantify changes in ecosystem carbon storage, which could result from a shift from beech to oak forests as a consequence of climate warming. We find that the ecosystem carbon pool is reduced by about 55 Mg C ha-1 upon the replacement of beech by oak forests, which could occur either naturally in the course of succession or due to the choice of more drought tolerant tree species by foresters.
